Change has been successfully merged
A fair bit of personal opinion enclosed.
Thanks for the review - I do appreciate the input, including the personal opinion!

I have pushed a new change here; I have marked some of the comments as done, but others just had responses from me. Feel free to either mark as resolved as you see fit, or follow up on the discussion.
Is there a reason to force base-16 on the UI?
More convention than anything else. The NCSI docs, as well as existing commands, all use hex for the opcode values, so this avoids requiring the user to add 0x all over the place.
Done

I would prefer the payload be represented on the command line as space delimited octets instead of a concatenated string of base-16 pairs that are hard to read and confirm correct.

Is there a compelling reason to maintain the, IMO.... impolite, model of ncsi_netlink? Can this wart be hidden from the user?

If there is a desire to keep the packed string, perhaps add a command line switch that reads octets?

Yeah, I'd agree that the payload format in `ncsi-netlink` is a bit awkward.

I could just autodetect a packed string vs. separate octets, would that suit? Would prefer to avoid an explicit argument (to define the format) if we can detect reliably.
OK, new change pushed that allows either format.
Why are you filling a std::shared with a std::unique?
Excellent question. I'll see if we still need the shared_ptr at all.
We can do this with just the unique_ptr, and prevent a couple of copies too.
why does OEM use `auto payload` and this pre-defines `payload`?
Because raw allows an empty payload, so we construct an empty one here, in case no payload argument was provided.
Done

follow OEM model?
`auto payload = ...`
We need to check the std::optional before assigning to `payload`, and (as above) fall back to the default (empty) payload if none was provided.
Done

Not following the logic here.
It would be nice if there were a comment indicating the theory...
OK, shall do!
Done

Did I misread the change?
Isn't this sent as -oem (i.e. 0x50) and the rest is just the packed string?

Not sure I 100% understand the question, but the first byte on the packed string argument is interpreted the opcode field (both before and after this change).

It has always been possible to use `-o` to send non-OEM commands, by specifying a value other than `50` as the first byte in the string.

I've tried to make this more explicit in the new `ncsi-cmd`, through the `oem` vs `raw` subcommands.
Done

Suggestion: summarily remove -o from ncsi-netlink, and print a "use ncsi-cmd" message.
The following code is kludgy...

It's kludgy, but temporary.

We need this so that we don't break things in the transition to `ncsi-cmd`. Once this change is merged, we can update the in-tree usage of `ncsi-netlink -o` to use `ncsi-cmd` directly, then remove the compatibility later.

That should be a fairly quick process, there are only a small number of instances where `ncsi-netlink -o` is used.
Done

I am not sure the consensus with the maintainers here is, but it would be a lot more easier to read if we used a CLI parser library like CLI11 (https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11). I know other openbmc repos use this. Reason I proposed this is because we have a lot of "sub-command" parsing in this source file which would be easily covered by a library.

I had definitely thought so when doing this change, but I'm just keeping consistent with the existing getopt() usage that already exists for the ncsi-netlink utility.

I'm happy to look at other options for parsing the command-line, especially as we grow support for new commands, but would rather do that as a separate series after merge.
Fair point. We can take that transition up later.
(nit) can we use std::stoul instead since we technically need the unsigned int?
good catch, and we should probably use an unsigned (plus a range check) for the EID parsing added later. Updated change coming shortly.
Done
Updated to use stoul for `parseUnsigned`.
Thanks for the review. I'll upload a next version with the return value fixed. Let me know if you want further changes on the ncsi-netlink backwards-compat args handling.
Do we need to check for the max size of the payload?

We should have a sensible limit already imposed based on maximum arg sizes; we don't have a specific limit here as the NCSI commands may be arbitrarily large.

We could add a limit here, but it would be fairly arbitrary.
Can we explicitly return the error code here?
Yes, definitely - this should be returning `EXIT_FAILURE`.
Done
Should we use the RAII?

Not sure what we'd need to initialise on acquisition here; the argv setup needs to be somewhat manual.

However, this should be fairly temporary code - we'll only need this until we have converted existing `ncsi-netlink` invocations to use `ncsi-cmd` instead, and there are only a couple of those. I will send those as a follow-up.
Makring as resolved, as I don't *think* this needs to be changed, but feel free to unresolve if you have a better implementation in mind.

Given this is ony short-term, I would prefer not to introduce extra infrastructure (in the `ArgvManager`) there.

If you're okay with merging as-is, that would be my preference.
Ack
Do we need to put any validation check around argv?
In the case of success we are not freeing the resources as it will be take care by the program tremination?
We should be fine; this path (intentionally) doesn't have any specific knowledge of the valid args here, and so should just pass directly to the execed process.

Sort of - the entire process' memory will be replaced on exec.

But more to the point: there is no way to run *any* code on a successful exec, as we're no longer running 😊
